title: Which place is richer?
hook: Find counts and search effort can differ.

knows: A rate compares a count with the amount searched.
doesNotKnow: Raw totals can change with search effort even when observed yield per site is equal.

misconception: More finds always mean more finds per searched site.
objective: Compute finds per site in two constructed surveys.

claims.text: In a hypothetical survey, A has two finds in two sites and B has eight finds in eight sites; each rate is one per site. A difference in raw totals can arise from unequal search effort, and equal observed rates do not establish equal true abundance.
claims.source: Arithmetic and declared constructed example; not field data.

claims.text: The stage is a schematic model, with stated example values or sample counts; it is not a reconstruction of an observed field site.
Recall: Survey X finds 3 fossils in 3 sites; survey Y finds 6 in 6. Which has the higher observed finds per site? Both rates are one find per searched site.
claims.source: Relative order or arithmetic under the explicitly stated example conditions.

recall.question: Survey X finds 3 fossils in 3 sites; survey Y finds 6 in 6. Which has the higher observed finds per site?
recall.why: Both rates are one find per searched site.
